summary: Fresh independent GENERAL review found a new blocker: the fresh-regression oracle rejects valid current pytest parameterized collection/JUnit evidence. Prior selector-coverage and integer-exit findings are resolved; scope, exact evidence bindings, legacy semantics and deferred layer dispositions remain preserved.

findings.title: Accept valid parameter IDs when correlating collection with JUnit
findings.body: The required fresh full-harness regression cannot validate existing successful pytest cases. Current real harness/unit collection has 25 parameter IDs containing :: inside brackets; line 2650 splits those parameter suffixes, whereas pytest partitions at [ before splitting and restores the complete suffix. On an otherwise valid full-command integrated Git fixture, replacing only the harness case with one actual current node ID and correct pytest JUnit addressing yields exactly milestone-m3-regression:incomplete-executed-collection. Lines 2645-2646 also scan node text for error/skip disposition words; current collected parameter text includes 1 error/1 skipped, and successful [1 skipped] parameter evidence yields exactly collection-oracle. Baseline validation returns no errors, and all hash/freshness, integer-zero, selector and successful-count guards pass in both reproductions. These false rejections block the mandatory integrated regression without changing frozen semantics.
findings.required_change: Normalize node addresses according to pytest parameter-aware JUnit addressing: split only the nonparameter address and preserve the entire bracket suffix. Check collection disposition/summary records separately from collected node content while retaining strict rejection of actual failures/errors/skips, incomplete selectors and case mismatches. Add real pytest-generated collection/JUnit positive coverage for parameter IDs containing :: and summary-looking words, plus the existing negative oracle coverage. Record new selected tested evidence and fresh exact-SHA reviews.
